title: Employee Mobility and Systems Access Framework
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary
This playbook defines a single, company-wide framework for (1) granting and revoking system access, (2) managing employee travel and mobility, and (3) standardizing procurement, vendor onboarding, and expense workflows. It consolidates existing practices into a cohesive reference intended for hiring managers, system owners, people-ops, security, finance, and employees who travel or contract vendors.

Purpose
- Reduce friction for legitimate business activity while maintaining least-privilege controls.
- Clarify responsibilities, SLAs, and templates for access requests, change approvals, procurements, and travel.
- Provide operational playbooks for emergency access, contractor offboarding, vendor assessments, and cross-border data handling.

Scope
Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors, vendors and contingent workers that interact with Redwood production or sensitive data. Components covered: IAM & permissions, temporary access (bastion/sudo), change management for infra and app-level changes, procurement (cards and POs), vendor onboarding & assessment, travel booking & reimbursable expenses, and internal templates.

Key Definitions
- System Owner: person accountable for access decisions on a service (usually the service lead or product manager).
- Requester: employee initiating an access/procurement/travel request.
- Approver: manager/role required by the workflow.
- Privileged Access: any access that allows production-side data exfiltration, administrative actions (root/sudo), secrets management, or billing.

Roles & Responsibilities
- People-Ops: policy owner, onboarding/offboarding orchestration, travel policy administration.
- Security: approves privileged access patterns, runs periodic access reviews, maintains exception register.
- Finance: approves procurement thresholds, conducts vendor payment setup.
- Managers (requester’s manager): approve routine access and travel.
- System Owners: approve service-level permissions, attest periodic access reviews.

Access & Permissions
Principles
1. Least privilege by default.
2. Temporary access for non-routine tasks.
3. Separation of duties: provisioning and approval should be distinct roles.

Access Request Process (standard flow)
1. Employee files request via Access Portal (Confluence form -> OKTA ticket).
2. Request must include purpose, duration, and scope (specific resources).
3. Manager approves (within 48 hours).
4. System Owner confirms service-level needs (SLA 3 business days).
5. Security performs a risk check if request involves Production or Sensitive data.

Approval Matrix (representative thresholds)
- Non-sensitive SaaS (e.g., Slack channels): manager approval.
- Internal dev environments: manager + system owner.
- Production access or secrets: manager + system owner + Security.
- Cross-account/cloud console access: manager + System Owner + SRE + Security.

Temporary Access Rules
- Default duration: 8 hours for ad-hoc troubleshooting, 30 days for development contractors.
- Extensions require renewal through the Access Portal with justification.
- All temporary sessions must be recorded (session recording where available) and audited weekly.

Privileged Key & Secret Management
- Secrets stored only in approved vaults (KMS/HSM + central secrets manager).
- Permanent secrets rotate every 90 days; service-account keys rotate every 60 days.
- No long-lived personal API keys for production.

Emergency (Break-glass) Access
1. Initiate incident channel and tag security on-call.
2. Security issues one-time elevated token via emergency delegation service (valid for 1 hour).
3. Requester documents actions within 24 hours and files a retrospective.

Periodic Reviews
- Quarterly access attestation: System Owners must confirm active users and roles.
- Monthly privileged user audit by Security.

Change Management
Change Types
- Routine: application config changes that do not touch production data (low risk).
- Standard: planned infra or app changes with predefined runbooks (medium risk).
- Emergency: changes necessary to remediate incidents (high risk).

Change Advisory Board (CAB)
- Weekly CAB for standard changes. Representation: Engineering (serving-runtime/infra), Security, SRE, Product.
- CAB template: change id, owner, start/end window, rollback plan, impact matrix, monitoring/alerts.

Change Workflow (standard change)
1. Submit RFC in the Change Portal with risk score and rollout plan.
2. Stakeholders comment within 48 hours.
3. CAB approves or requests mitigation steps.
4. Deploy during agreed maintenance window.
5. Post-deploy verification and rollback capability confirmed.

Rollback & Postmortem
- Every standard and emergency change must include a clear rollback plan.
- If an emergency change occurs, a postmortem indexed in Confluence must be filed within 5 business days.

Change Exceptions
- Exceptions are timeboxed and recorded in the Access Exception Registry with an owner and an expiry (max 30 days unless reapproved).

Data Management
Data Classification
- Public: information safe to disclose.
- Internal: non-sensitive company data.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, regulated info, or secrets.

Handling Rules
- Restricted data requires encryption at rest and in transit, access limited to approved roles, and cannot be stored in personal cloud drives.
- Cross-border transfer of Restricted data requires Legal sign-off and documented data flow map.

Retention & Deletion
- Default retention: product logs 90 days, backups 180 days unless business/legal require longer.
- Data deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) workflow in the Privacy Portal.

Backups & Recovery
- Backups must be encrypted, stored in a separate account, and tested quarterly for restore capability.

Procurement & Expenses
Procurement Routing
- Low-value purchases (< $2,500): corporate card or manager approval.
- Mid-value purchases ($2,500–$50,000): Procurement Request (PR) + Finance Manager approval.
- High-value purchases (> $50,000): PR + Finance Director + VP approval; competitive quotes required.

Purchase Process
1) Create PR with line items, business justification, budget code, and vendor contact.
2) Procurement verifies supplier PO terms and conflict-of-interest checks.
3) Finance approves and issues PO or instructs corporate card charge.

Expense Reimbursement
- Use Expense System with photographed receipts. Meals per diem: domestic $75/day, international varies by region (see Expense Matrix link).
- Per diem and lodging max rates published annually.

Corporate Cards & Controls
- Cardholders have monthly limits set by Finance. Card transactions over $5,000 require pre-authorization.
- Misuse results in revocation and HR disciplinary review.

Vendor Management
Onboarding Checklist
1) Business justification & approved PO.
2) Security assessment: questionnaire covering SOC2/ISO, data handling, penetration testing history.
3) Legal review & signed contract (includes security addendum).
4) Finance vendor setup and tax forms.

Third-Party Risk Assessment
- Vendors categorized by access & data exposure (Low, Medium, High).
- High-risk vendors require annual security attestation, penetration test evidence, and right-to-audit clauses.

Contract SLAs & Escalation
- Contracts > $100k or >12 months must include SLA metrics (uptime, response time), financial remedies, and an executive escalation path.

Vendor Offboarding
- Deprovision access within 24 hours of contract end.
- Reclaim assets and ensure data destruction or return per contract.

Travel & Employee Mobility
Booking and Approval
- Employees request travel via Travel Portal with manager approval. Travel booking must use preferred vendors for negotiated rates.
- Non-standard travel requires pre-approval from Finance and People-Ops.

Safety & Duty of Care
- People-Ops publishes travel advisories. Employees must register international travel and carry emergency contact info.
- For high-risk locations, security will require a travel safety plan and may restrict travel.

Reimbursement & Allowed Expenses
- Reimbursable: airfare (economy or business for flights >6 hours with manager approval), lodging, ground transport, meals (see per diem).
- Non-reimbursable: in-room entertainment, personal expenses, fines.

Remote Work & Mobility
- For long-term remote work or relocation, use the Remote Work Request form: includes stipend, hardware shipping, tax implications, and local labor compliance checks.

Templates & Examples
Included templates (attached as documents in the Confluence page):
- Access Request form (fields: requester, manager, system, scope, duration, business justification).
- Change Request (RFC) template with risk score and rollback plan.
- Procurement Request template (line items, budget, vendor).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSAQ) checklist.
- Travel Pre-approval & Expense form.

Example: Minimal Access Request (copy/paste)
```
Requester: Priya.Shah@redwood.com
Manager: Maria.Gupta@redwood.com
System: analytics-reporting-prod
Scope: read-only on analytics schema; no export
Duration: 14 days
Business justification: validate report queries for Q4 billing reconciliation
```

Enforcement & Exceptions
- Non-compliance discovered during audit will trigger remediation steps: 1) immediate revocation if critical; 2) remediation plan within 5 business days; 3) disciplinary review if repeated misuse.
- Exception process: submit Exception Request with scope, owner, compensating controls, and expiry. Security reviews exceptions monthly.

Metrics & Reporting
- Monthly reports: number of open access requests, average approval time, number of privileged accounts, vendor risk distribution.
- Quarterly KPIs: mean time to grant access (target <72 hours), privileged access reduction (target -10% year/year).

Appendix A — Contacts and Escalation Points
- People-Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security On-call: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Travel Desk: travel@redwood.com

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets and sample policy (service account rotation)
- Rotate key (example): 
ssh into key-rotation-host && ./rotate_service_key --service analytics --env prod --rotate-days 60

- Sample retention YAML (apply in infra repo):
retention:
  logs_days: "90"
  backups_days: "180"
  sensitive_data_flag: "true"

Change Log
- 2028-11-07: Created by Priya Shah (people-ops).
- 2029-02-13: Revised procurement thresholds and travel per diem schedule; added vendor offboarding SLA.
